title: objectql/driver-sql: a multi-valued relation's nested-relation condition as an in-database JSON-membership semi-join (no 1000-id cap)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1QwJJ5KGZTThP4fnq

Follow-up of #33626 (draft PR #33652). ⛔ Not a claim.

## What exists

After #33652 a single-valued relation's nested-relation condition on a read verb is one in-database subquery. A multi-valued relation (`multiple: true`, stored as a JSON id list) still reads the related ids first and lowers to an `$or` of one `$contains` per id, capped at `RELATION_FILTER_ID_CAP` (1000): `{ owners: { region: 'CAP' } }` with 1001 matching owners answers `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 (pinned in `packages/rest/src/data-nested-object-door.test.ts`, "no cap on a single-valued relation … a multi-valued one past the cap is REFUSED").

## What lands

A membership semi-join on the SQL drivers: a row is selected when ANY member of its JSON id list is in the related object's planned, read-scoped subquery — e.g. an `EXISTS` over the dialect's JSON array expansion (SQLite `json_each`, PostgreSQL `jsonb_array_elements_text`, MySQL `JSON_TABLE`, SQL Server `OPENJSON`), joined to `IN (SELECT id …)` with the tenant wall. Same NULL / empty-list / unreadable-member semantics as the id route; parity tests against the two-step route per dialect.

## Open point for the implementer

How a `ReadableIds` leaf is spelled against a JSON list column (today the SQL family refuses `$in` over it) is a driver-contract question under ADR-0139; if it needs a new leaf form, stop and return `needs_decision`.

## Grade

p2. Same downstream pull as #33626 for dashboards over multi-valued relations.
